newsitem.title: USA: Fat Tuesday Paczki fever strikes Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Fat Tuesday Paczki fever strikes Chicago.

text.p: Chicagoans lined up outside bakeries at dawn on Tuesday to buy "paczkis" -- large, buttery Polish pastries eaten the day before Lent begins.
"At 5:30 to quarter to six this morning customers were banging on the doors," said Norm Dinkel, owner of Dinkel's Bakery. "They're buying them by the dozens."

To meet Chicago's voracious appetite for the Fat Tuesday treat -- pronounced "punch-key" -- 10 bakers had been at work since 4 a.m. Monday at Gladstone's Bakery in Chicago to make 18,000 of the pastries, owner Vinnie Zygman said.
"If they keep moving like they have been, we'll sell out by this afternoon," Zygman added. "Last year we sold out early, so this year we made 3,000 more."
Polish bakers first began making the big pastries, filled with custard, jam or fruit, to empty their larders before Lent, the Christian season of fasting before Easter.
Chicago's large Polish communities are the largest consumers of paczkis, and their popularity has grown tremendously over the last decade, bakers said.
